questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked

Real-world cross-cloud serverless platforms demand automated image signing and artifact attestations. This question tests end-to-end workflow design, policy enforcement decisions, and practical CI/CD integration skills.

## Key Concepts

- Cosign signing and verification
- Rekor attestations for transparency and auditability
- SBOM generation (using tools like Syft)
- Multi-cloud serverless deployment patterns
- GitHub Actions workflow integration

## Code Example

```yaml
name: cks-serverless-sign
on:
  pull_request:
    types: [opened, synchronize]

jobs:
  gate:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Install cosign
        uses: sigstore/cosign-installer@v3

      - name: Set up Syft for SBOM
        uses: anchore/syft-action@v1

      - name: Build and push image
        run: |
          docker build -t ${{ vars.REGISTRY }}/serverless-fn:${{ github.sha }} .
          docker push ${{ vars.REGISTRY }}/serverless-fn:${{ github.sha }}

      - name: Generate SBOM
        run: |
          syft ${{ vars.REGISTRY }}/serverless-fn:${{ github.sha }} -o cyclonedx-json > sbom.json

      - name: Sign image with cosign
        run: |
          cosign sign --key cosign.key ${{ vars.REGISTRY }}/serverless-fn:${{ github.sha }}

      - name: Verify signature
        run: |
          cosign verify --key cosign.pub ${{ vars.REGISTRY }}/serverless-fn:${{ github.sha }}

      - name: Upload to Rekor
        run: |
          cosign upload blob -f attestation.json
```

## Failing Manifest (Unsigned Image)

```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: serverless-workload
spec:
  containers:
  - name: function
    image: registry.example.com/serverless-fn:abc123
```

## Passing Manifest (Signed Image)

```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: serverless-workload
spec:
  containers:
  - name: function
    image: registry.example.com/serverless-fn:signed-sha256
    imagePullPolicy: Always
```

## Local Verification

```bash
# Verify image signature
cosign verify --key cosign.pub registry.example.com/serverless-fn:signed-sha256

# Verify attestation
cosign verify-attestation --type cyclonedx --key cosign.pub registry.example.com/serverless-fn:signed-sha256
```

## CI Verification Steps

1. Add Cosign verification step in CI pipeline
2. Block deployment if signature verification fails
3. Verify SBOM matches image contents
4. Check Rekor transparency log for attestation

# Kyverno policy example
apiVersion: kyverno.io/v1
kind: ClusterPolicy
metadata:

spec:
  validationFailureAction: audit
  rules:

package gatekeeper

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Fintech workloads handling sensitive financial data demand strict data-protection posture. This question validates your understanding of end-to-end security enforcement—from CI gates that catch misconfigurations before deployment to runtime policies that protect running workloads.

## Key Concepts
- CI gate for manifest validation at pull request stage
- Resource requests/limits for resource governance
- readOnlyRootFilesystem for filesystem security
- TLS secret mounting with tls-cert-<app> naming convention
- Runtime policy enforcement via Kyverno or OPA
- Verification strategies for both CI and cluster runtime

## Code Example
```yaml
# Kyverno ClusterPolicy
apiVersion: kyverno.io/v1
kind: ClusterPolicy
metadata:
  name: require-secure-deploy
spec:
  rules:
  - name: enforce-resources-readonly
    match:
      resources:
        kinds:
        - Deployment
        - Pod
    validate:
      message: "Deployment must set resources.limits, resources.requests, and readOnlyRootFilesystem: true"
      pattern:
        spec:
          template:
            spec:
              securityContext:
                readOnlyRootFilesystem: "true"
              containers:
              - resources:
                  limits:
                    memory: "?*"
                    cpu: "?*"
                  requests:
                    memory: "?*"
                    cpu: "?*"
  - name: enforce-tls-secret-mount
    match:
      resources:
        kinds:
        - Pod
    validate:
      message: "TLS secret must be mounted at /etc/tls from Secret tls-cert-<app>"
      pattern:
        spec:
          volumes:
          - secret:
              secretName: tls-cert-?*
              items:
              - key: tls.crt
                path: etc/tls/tls.crt
```

## Sample Compliant Manifest
```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Secret
metadata:
  name: tls-cert-payment-service
type: kubernetes.io/tls
data:
  tls.crt: <base64-cert>
  tls.key: <base64-key>
---
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: payment-service
spec:
  replicas: 2
  template:
    spec:
      securityContext:
        readOnlyRootFilesystem: true
      containers:
      - name: app
        image: payment-service:latest
        resources:
          limits:
            memory: "512Mi"
            cpu: "500m"
          requests:
            memory: "256Mi"
            cpu: "250m"
        volumeMounts:
        - name: tls-certs
          mountPath: /etc/tls
          readOnly: true
      volumes:
      - name: tls-certs
        secret:
          secretName: tls-cert-payment-service
```

## Sample Non-Compliant Manifest
```yaml
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: insecure-service
spec:
  replicas: 2
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: app
        image: insecure-service:latest
        # Missing: resources.limits/requests
        # Missing: readOnlyRootFilesystem
        # Missing: TLS secret mount
```

## GitHub Actions CI Gate
```yaml
name: Security Gate
on: [pull_request]
jobs:
  security-check:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
    - uses: actions/checkout@v4
    - name: Install kubeval
      run: |4
        curl -L -o kubeval https://github.com/instrumenta/kubeval/releases/latest/download/kubeval-linux-amd64.tar.gz
        tar xf kubeval-linux-amd64.tar.gz
        sudo mv kubeval /usr/local/bin
    - name: Validate manifests
      run: |
        for f in k8s/*.yaml; do
          kubeval --strict --additional-schema-locations=https://kubernetesjsonschema.dev $f || exit 1
        done
    - name: Check resource limits
      run: |
        yq -e '.spec.template.spec.containers[].resources.limits' k8s/*.yaml || exit 1
    - name: Check readOnlyRootFilesystem
      run: |
        yq -e '.spec.template.spec.securityContext.readOnlyRootFilesystem == true' k8s/*.yaml || exit 1
    - name: Check TLS secret mounting
      run: |
        yq -e '.spec.template.spec.volumes[].secret.secretName | test("^tls-cert-")' k8s/*.yaml || exit 1
```

## Verification Steps

### CI Verification
1. Create a PR with the non-compliant manifest—pipeline should fail
2. Update to compliant manifest—pipeline should pass
3. Confirm all three checks (resources, readOnlyRootFilesystem, TLS) are enforced

### Runtime Verification
1. Apply Kyverno policy to test cluster
2. Attempt to deploy non-compliant manifest—deployment should be blocked
3. Verify policy logs show rejection reason
4. Apply compliant manifest—deployment should succeed

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Tests practical data validation in CI/CD with a concrete schema and gating.

## Key Concepts
- CSV header validation
- Type coercion and data quality
- CI gate integration (GitHub Actions)

## Code Example
```python
import csv, sys
from datetime import datetime

EXPECTED = {
  'id': int,
  'date': 'date',
  'amount': float,
  'category': str
}

DATE_FMT = '%Y-%m-%d'

def parse_row(row):
  row['id'] = int(row['id'])
  row['date'] = datetime.strptime(row['date'], DATE_FMT).date()
  row['amount'] = float(row['amount'])
  row['category'] = str(row['category'])
  return row

def main(path):
  with open(path, newline='') as f:
    reader = csv.DictReader(f)
    header = set(reader.fieldnames or [])
    if header != set(EXPECTED.keys()):
      print('Header mismatch:', reader.fieldnames)
      sys.exit(1)
    for r in reader:
      try:
        parse_row(r)
      except Exception as e:
        print('Type/Parse error', e, r)
        sys.exit(1)
  print('OK')

if __name__ == '__main__':
  sys.exit(main(sys.argv[1]))
```

- How would you test locally with representative failing/passing CSVs?

questions.explanation:
## Why This Question Is Asked

This question evaluates expertise in multi-cloud tenancy, data residency compliance, and automated policy enforcement. It requires understanding of cross-cloud networking, secret management patterns, service mesh security, and continuous verification using Prometheus. Candidates must demonstrate end-to-end enforcement—from namespace isolation through egress traffic, mTLS, and progressive delivery.

## Key Concepts

- **Cross-cloud tenancy isolation**: Enforcing hard boundaries between tenants across AWS, GCP, and Azure requires consistent policy engines that understand region semantics and cloud-specific resource constraints.

- **Admission control patterns**: Kyverno excels at mutation and generation, while OPA Gatekeeper provides robust enforce-or-deny semantics. Using both in concert allows for defense-in-depth.

- **Secret management**: Preventing literal secrets in environment variables and enforcing SecretStore references is critical for security compliance in regulated environments.

- **Network policy enforcement**: Per-tenant egress gateways with namespace-aware NetworkPolicies ensure traffic cannot leak across tenant boundaries.

```yaml
# .github/workflows/pin-digest.yml
name: Pin Image Digests
on:
  push:
    paths:
      - '**/*.yaml'
      - '**/*.yml'
jobs:
  digest_check:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v3
      - name: Install jq and yq
        run: sudo apt-get update && sudo apt-get install -y jq wget
      - name: Install yq
        run: wget -qO- https://github.com/mikefarah/yq/releases/download/v4.25.1/yq_linux_amd64 -O /usr/bin/yq && chmod +x /usr/bin/yq
      - name: Validate image digests
        run: |
          DIGESTED=$(yq -r '.. | .image? // empty' **/*.yaml **/*.yml | grep -v '^$' )
          if echo "$DIGESTED" | grep -vq '@sha256:'; then
            echo "Found image refs without digest:";
            echo "$DIGESTED"; exit 1;
          fi
          echo "All images pinned to digests."
```

## Why This Is Asked
Security hardening of Kubernetes manifests is a practical, repeatable gate in real projects. This tests understanding of policy-as-code, tooling choices (Kyverno vs Gatekeeper), constraint design for host access controls and image source controls, and CI integration in GitHub Actions with ephemeral test clusters.

## Key Concepts
- Policy-as-code with Kyverno or OPA Gatekeeper
- Constraints for host access (hostNetwork, hostPath, hostPort, privileged containers)
- Image source controls (allowed registries) and imagePullPolicy enforcement
- CI integration in GitHub Actions using KinD or similar ephemeral clusters

## Code Example
```yaml
apiVersion: kyverno.io/v1
kind: ClusterPolicy
metadata:
  name: deny-host-access
spec:
  rules:
  - name: block-host-network
    match:
      resources:
        kinds:
        - Pod
    validate:
      message: "hostNetwork is not allowed"
      pattern:
        spec:
          hostNetwork: "false"
  - name: block-host-path
    match:
      resources:
        kinds:
        - Pod
    validate:
      message: "hostPath volumes are not allowed"
      deny:
        conditions:
        - key: "{{ contains(element.volumes[].hostPath, '') }}"
          operator: "NotEqual"
          value: ""
```

## Minimal Policy (Combined)
```yaml
apiVersion: kyverno.io/v1
kind: ClusterPolicy
metadata:
  name: security-guardrails
spec:
  rules:
  - name: deny-host-network-port
    match:
      resources:
        kinds:
        - Pod
    validate:
      message: "hostNetwork and hostPort are not permitted"
      pattern:
        spec:
          hostNetwork: "false"
          hostPort: "0"
  - name: deny-host-path
    match:
      resources:
        kinds:
        - Pod
    validate:
      message: "hostPath volumes are not permitted"
      deny:
        conditions:
        - key: "{{ @ }}"
          operator: "AnyNotIn"
          value: [""]
      foreach:
        - list: "spec.volumes[?hostPath]"
          deny: true
  - name: deny-privileged-containers
    match:
      resources:
        kinds:
        - Pod
    validate:
      message: "Privileged containers are not permitted"
      pattern:
        spec:
          containers:
          - securityContext:
              privileged: "false"
  - name: allowed-registries
    match:
      resources:
        kinds:
        - Pod
    validate:
      message: "Images must come from approved registries"
      pattern:
        spec:
          containers:
          - image: "registry.company.com/*"
            imagePullPolicy: "Always"
```

## Failing Manifest (hostPath + hostNetwork)
```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: insecure-pod
spec:
  hostNetwork: true
  containers:
  - name: app
    image: docker.io/myapp:latest
    securityContext:
      privileged: true
    volumeMounts:
    - name: host-volume
      mountPath: /data
  volumes:
  - name: host-volume
    hostPath:
      path: /etc
```

## Passing Manifest
```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: secure-pod
spec:
  containers:
  - name: app
    image: registry.company.com/myapp:v1.0
    imagePullPolicy: Always
```

## Local Validation
```bash
# Install Kyverno locally
brew install kyverno

# Apply policies
kubectl apply -f security-guardrails.yaml

# Validate a manifest
kyverno validate insecure-pod.yaml
```

## CI Validation (GitHub Actions)
```yaml
name: Validate Manifests
on: [pull_request]
jobs:
  validate:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
    - uses: actions/checkout@v4
    - name: Create KinD cluster
      run: kind create cluster
    - name: Install Kyverno
      run: |
        kubectl apply -f https://github.com/kyverno/kyverno/releases/latest/download/install.yaml
        kubectl wait --for=condition=ready pod -l app=kyverno -n kyverno --timeout=120s
    - name: Apply policies
      run: kubectl apply -f security-guardrails.yaml
    - name: Validate manifests
      run: |
        kubectl apply --dry-run=server -f insecure-pod.yaml || echo "Expected failure"
        kubectl apply --dry-run=server -f secure-pod.yaml
```

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
This checks namespace discipline and registry trust in manifests, a common pitfall in multi-environment apps.

## Key Concepts
- YAML manifest parsing (basic PyYAML)
- Simple allowlists for namespaces and image registries
- Tag validation (reject :latest)
- CI gate integration (GitHub Actions)

## Code Example
```python
# manifestlint.py
import yaml, sys
ALLOWED_NS = {"dev","staging","prod"}
ALLOWED_REG = {"registry.trusted"}

def ok(manifest):
  docs = yaml.safe_load_all(manifest)
  for m in docs or []:
    if m.get("kind") in {"Deployment","StatefulSet","DaemonSet"}:
      ns = m.get("metadata", {}).get("namespace")
      if ns not in ALLOWED_NS:
        return False
      for c in m.get("spec", {}).get("template", {}).get("spec", {}).get("containers", []):
        img = c.get("image", "")
        if not any(img.startswith(r) for r in ALLOWED_REG) or ":latest" in img:
          return False
  return True

if __name__ == '__main__':
  path = sys.argv[1]
  with open(path) as f:
    print(ok(f.read()))
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you adapt for Helm templating?  
- How would you run this as a pre-commit hook?

## Why This Is Asked
Tests understanding of Gatekeeper policy design, basic Rego, and CI validation.

## Key Concepts
- OPA Gatekeeper, ConstraintTemplate, Constraint, Rego basics
- Pod security: runAsNonRoot, readOnlyRootFilesystem, image allowlists
- CI integration and local validation strategies

## Code Example
```yaml
# ConstraintTemplate (conceptual)
apiVersion: templates.gatekeeper.sh/v1beta1
kind: ConstraintTemplate
metadata:
  name: k8spodsecurity
spec:
  crd:
    spec:
      names:
        kind: K8SPodSecurity
  targets:
  - target: admission.k8s.gatekeeper.sh
    rego: |
      package k8spodsecurity
      # policy consolidated in real template
```
```yaml
# Constraint (conceptual)
apiVersion: constraints.gatekeeper.sh/v1beta1
kind: K8SPodSecurity
spec:
  match:
    kinds:
      - apiGroups: ["apps"]
        kinds: ["Deployment"]
  parameters:
    allowList:
      - registry.example.com/*
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you handle per-environment allowlists?
- How would you audit Gatekeeper decisions historically?

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Tests practical hardening policies across CI and runtime, not just definitions.

## Key Concepts
- Kyverno policy drafting, matches, and deny rules
- Pod security basics: readOnlyRootFilesystem, allowPrivilegeEscalation, capabilities
- CI/CD integration and runtime admission flow; namespace-based exceptions

## Code Example
```yaml
apiVersion: kyverno.io/v1
kind: ClusterPolicy
metadata:
  name: require-container-hardening
spec:
  validationFailureAction: fail
  rules:
  - name: deny-privileged-containers
    match:
      resources:
        kinds: ["Pod"]
    deny:
    - conditions:
      - key: '{{request.object.spec.containers[*].securityContext.privileged}}'
        operator: Equals
        value: 'true'
  - name: enforce-secure-rootfs
    match:
      resources:
        kinds: ["Pod"]
    deny:
    - conditions:
      - key: '{{request.object.spec.containers[*].securityContext.readOnlyRootFilesystem}}'
        operator: NotIn
        value: ['true']
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you test namespace-level exemptions?
- How would you surface policy violations in CI dashboards and alerts?

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked

Tests ability to design policy-as-code for cross-cloud data residency in ML workloads, a real-world constraint.

## Key Concepts

- Data residency across regions
- CMK encryption for secrets
- DataPolicy CRD and audit sink
- Admission control with Kyverno/OPA
- CI verification strategy

## Code Example

```yaml
# Kyverno policy snippet (illustrative)
apiVersion: kyverno.io/v1
kind: ClusterPolicy
metadata:
  name: data-residency
spec:
  rules:
  - name: require-region-bound-storage
    match:
      resources:
        kinds:
        - Pod
    validate:
      message: data-residency violation
      pattern:
        spec:
          volumes:
          - name: '*'
```

```rego
# OPA/Gatekeeper style policy (illustrative)
package dataresidency
violation:[{'msg':'volume region not allowed'}] {
  input.review.kind.kind == 'Pod'
  not allowed_region(input.review.object.spec.volumes[_].region)
}
allowed_region(r) { r == 'us-east-1'; r == 'eu-west-1' }
```

## Follow-up Questions

- How would you test region migrations and audit data movement?
- How would you monitor policy coverage over time?
